eta.notes: Sistema de Autorización Electrónica (SAE) - electronic travel authorization required now to board air travel to Mexico. Air travel only; single entry; authorization valid 30 days from issuance; immigration officer may authorize up to 180 days stay at the port of entry. Land and sea entry require a traditional consular visa. (verified 2026-07)

cbi.notes: Mexico does not have an official Citizenship by Investment (CBI) program, and a fresh check as of August 2026 found no proposed or enacted CBI-style scheme (no Argentina-style saga exists here) - confirmed by the absence of any official CBI program on gob.mx, INM, or SRE portals, and corroborated by multiple independent industry sources. Investment can lead to Temporary Residency (and later Permanent Residency), which after the legally required period can lead to naturalization. The naturalization route itself (Ley de Nacionalidad, Art. 20) is generous relative to peers and more tiered than a single number suggests: 5 years of residency for the general case (Art. 20 chapeau); cut to 2 years for spouses of Mexican nationals (Art. 20-II, 2 years of cohabitation at a shared domicile) and for nationals of Latin American or Iberian Peninsula countries (Art. 20-I(c)) - Argentine, Spanish, and other Ibero-American passport holders qualify for the 2-year track; cut to just 1 year for adoptees and minors under the patria potestad of a Mexican national (Art. 20-III); and the President may waive the residency requirement entirely for applicants with notable scientific, artistic, sporting or business contributions to the nation (Art. 20-I(d)). A Spanish-language exam plus a basic Mexican history/culture exam is mandatory (Ley Art. 19-III + Reglamento Art. 14), waived to Spanish-only for refugees, minors, and applicants 60 or older. The process is entirely administrative, handled by SRE (Direccion de Nacionalidad), never a court - a clean contrast with Argentina, where the equivalent process is constitutionally judicial and, as of mid-2026, in active legal dispute over an attempt to make it administrative instead (see ARG.json). A 2026 SRE procedural reform targets 40 business days instead of the prior 90-day goal, per secondary reporting; the underlying DOF publication was not independently located, so treat the new turnaround target as reported-but-not-primary-sourced. The naturalization application fee is MXN $9,500 (Anexo 4, Resolucion Miscelanea Fiscal para 2026, valid Jan 1 - Dec 31 2026), confirmed on two official SRE fee pages; its exact Ley Federal de Derechos article citation could not be independently confirmed. Dual citizenship has been permitted since the 1998 constitutional reform (Art. 32) with no renunciation required, except for a short list of reserved public offices (President, cabinet secretaries, military officer corps, etc.), which are reserved for Mexican-by-birth nationals regardless. Naturalized citizenship can be revoked by SRE (an administrative resolution, with a SEGOB opinion and a hearing for the affected person first) for causes including voluntarily acquiring a foreign nationality, holding oneself out as a foreigner, or residing abroad 5+ continuous years - the exact Ley de Nacionalidad article numbers for this chapter could not be independently confirmed this pass (primary text blocked by bot-protection on repeated fetch attempts) and should be re-verified before citing a specific article number. Source: https://www.gob.mx/sre/acciones-y-programas/naturalizacion-de-extranjeros ; https://portales.sre.gob.mx/tramites-dgaj/naturalizacion/carta-de-naturalizacion-por-residencia ; https://portales.sre.gob.mx/tramites-dgaj/nacionalidad/costos-de-servicios-de-nacionalidad-y-naturalizacion

programs.name: Temporary Resident Visa for Investors
programs.notes: Investment must exceed 45,850 days of UMA. As of February 1, 2026 the daily UMA value is MXN $117.31 (confirmed by INEGI), giving a threshold of approximately MXN $5,378,663. Investment can be demonstrated through: (1) equity interest/shares in a Mexican company; (2) movable or fixed assets for business purposes; or (3) evidence of Mexican economic activity employing at least 3 workers. Visa grants stay of more than 180 days and up to 4 years. Must apply for Temporary Resident Card at INM within 30 days of arrival. path_to_citizenship_years reflects the general naturalization path (Ley de Nacionalidad Art. 20): 5 years of legal residency (temporary or permanent status both count) immediately preceding the application. Nationals of Latin American/Iberian Peninsula countries, or applicants married to a Mexican national, qualify for a reduced 2-year path instead (Art. 20-I(c) and 20-II) - see cbi.notes.

programs.name: Temporary Resident Visa - Economic Solvency (Rentista)
programs.notes: For retirees or those with passive income. CORRECTED August 2026: a new set of Lineamientos published in the DOF on July 25, 2025 (effective ~August 9, 2025) replaced the prior 2014 thresholds - the figures previously recorded here (400 / 20,000 / 40,000 UMA-days) are now stale and have been superseded. Current official requirements, re-verified directly against the cited source page: average monthly income, free of taxes, equivalent to 680 days of UMA (~MXN $79,771, ~USD $4,570/month at current UMA/FX) sustained over the last 6 months, OR an average monthly bank/investment balance equivalent to 11,460 days of UMA (~MXN $1,344,373, ~USD $77,015) averaged over the last 12 months. The prior real-estate-ownership alternative (previously ~40,000 UMA-days) no longer appears on the official page and should be treated as discontinued unless independently re-confirmed. Grants temporary residency for up to 4 years. path_to_citizenship_years is the general 5-year naturalization path (Ley de Nacionalidad Art. 20); reduced to 2 years for spouses of Mexican nationals or nationals of Latin American/Iberian Peninsula countries, 1 year for adoptees/minors under a Mexican national's patria potestad - see cbi.notes for the full naturalization framework, including the mandatory Spanish + history/culture exam and dual-citizenship rules.

programs.name: Permanent Resident Visa - Economic Solvency
programs.notes: Permanent Residence Visa by Economic Solvency requires investment receipts or bank statements showing an average monthly overall balance of over $292,859 USD per month (12 months of statements required). Grants indefinite right to reside in Mexico.

programs.name: Temporary Resident Visa (Remote Worker / Digital Nomad pathway)
programs.eligibility: Foreign nationals with income from sources outside Mexico. Must demonstrate: monthly income of at least approximately $3,737.95 USD for the past 6 months OR savings of approximately $73,257.65 USD for the past 12 months (amounts derived from UMA-based thresholds reported by official consulates). Must apply at a Mexican consulate abroad before entering Mexico.
programs.processing_time: Same day to 10 business days at consulate
programs.notes: Mexico has no separately named 'digital nomad visa'. Remote workers use the standard Temporary Resident Visa (Residente Temporal). Income must come from outside Mexico. No minimum physical presence requirement. Renewable annually up to 4 years total. After 4 years can apply for Permanent Residency.

The SRE Guia del Viajero provides individual country-by-country fichas (fact sheets) for Mexican travelers. The site was inaccessible to automated scraping during this session due to Radware bot protection on the portales.sre.gob.mx domain; the guiadelviajero.sre.gob.mx subdomain (older URL) also returned ECONNREFUSED. Country list is compiled from: (1) SRE official PDF listing countries requiring a visa from Mexicans (USA, Canada eTA, Cuba tourist card, China, Egypt, Russia, Thailand, Turkey e-visa, Australia); (2) individual Guia del Viajero country page snippets retrieved via web search (Portugal, Argentina, Netherlands, Dominica, Serbia, Montenegro, North Macedonia, South Korea, Seychelles); (3) SRE Mexico Embassy in Serbia page listing visa-free entry for Mexico citizens. Canada requires an ETA (Autorizacion Electronica/eTA, CAD 7) for air travel; Cuba requires a Tourist Card (Tarjeta de Turismo); USA and China require prior consular visa; Australia requires a subclass 600 visitor visa applied online. The full definitive list should be verified directly at portales.sre.gob.mx/guiadeviaje when the site is accessible.

visa_types.name: Visitor Visa - Non-Lucrative (Visa de Visitante sin Permiso para Realizar Actividades Remuneradas)
visa_types.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to visit Mexico as non-lucrative visitors for tourism, transit, business meetings, press/correspondent assignments, studies, or medical treatment without engaging in paid activities. Covers activities that do not generate income within Mexico.
visa_types.notes: Citizens of 50+ nationalities are visa-exempt and may enter without a visa for up to 180 days. Those requiring a visa must apply at a Mexican consulate. Immigration officer determines the exact authorized stay up to 180 days. FMM card issued at land borders must be retained for departure. UK temporary residents (students, workers) who are not permanent residents must apply for this visa even if their nationality is on the visa-free list. The official consulate source page explicitly lists 'correspondent' alongside tourism, business, transit, studies, and medical treatment as covered non-lucrative visitor purposes (verified 2026-07).

visa_types.name: Visitor Visa - Business (Visa de Visitante con Permiso para Realizar Actividades Remuneradas)
visa_types.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to enter Mexico to carry out paid or lucrative activities on a temporary basis, such as short-term contracts, conferences, or professional services paid from abroad.
visa_types.notes: This category authorizes remunerated activities during the visitor stay. Applicants must demonstrate the purpose of the visit and source of remuneration. Issued at Mexican consulates abroad. For stays intended to exceed 180 days or for full employment in Mexico, a Temporary Resident Visa with work authorization is required instead.

visa_types.name: Transit Visitor Visa (Visa de Visitante en Tránsito)
visa_types.purpose: Permits foreign nationals to transit through Mexico en route to a third country, covering layovers or brief stops that require passing through Mexican immigration.
visa_types.notes: Visa-exempt nationals do not require a transit visa. Citizens of nationalities that require a visa must obtain one prior to transit. Transit visas are covered under the Visitor Visa framework in Mexico's Ley de Migración. The standard non-lucrative visitor visa also covers transit purposes for those who require a visa.

visa_types.name: Temporary Resident Visa - Studies (Residente Temporal - Estudiante)
visa_types.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to reside in Mexico for the purpose of studying at an accredited educational institution for a period exceeding 180 days.
visa_types.notes: Issued for stays exceeding 180 days and up to 4 years (annual renewals). Requires acceptance letter from a Mexican educational institution. Holder must apply for a Temporary Resident Card (Tarjeta de Residente Temporal) at INM within 30 days of arrival. Short-term study programs of up to 180 days may use the non-lucrative visitor visa instead.

visa_types.name: Temporary Resident Visa with Authorization for Paid Activities (Residente Temporal con Permiso para Realizar Actividades Remuneradas)
visa_types.purpose: Allows foreign nationals to reside in Mexico and engage in paid employment or professional activities under a Mexican employer or contract for stays exceeding 180 days.
visa_types.notes: Requires an offer of employment or contract from a Mexican company. The employer typically initiates the process with INM to obtain a work authorization (oficio de autorización) before the applicant applies at the consulate. Issued for up to 1 year, renewable annually up to 4 years total. Holder must register at INM within 30 days of arrival for Temporary Resident Card.

visa_types.name: Temporary Resident Visa - Remote Worker / Digital Nomad (Residente Temporal - Solvencia Económica)
visa_types.purpose: Allows foreign nationals with income from outside Mexico to reside in the country for more than 180 days without taking local employment, serving as the de facto digital nomad pathway.
visa_types.notes: Mexico has no separately named digital nomad visa. Remote workers apply for the standard Temporary Resident Visa under economic solvency. Requirements: minimum monthly income of approximately $3,738 USD (equivalent to ~400 UMA days/month based on UMA $117.31/day as of February 2026) evidenced for 6 months, OR savings of approximately $73,258 USD. Income must originate from outside Mexico. Valid for 1 year, renewable annually up to 4 years. No minimum presence requirement.

visa_types.name: Temporary Resident Visa - Rentista / Economic Solvency (Residente Temporal - Solvencia Económica / Rentista)
visa_types.purpose: Allows retirees and persons with passive income or sufficient assets to reside in Mexico on a temporary basis without working locally.
visa_types.notes: Financial requirements (based on UMA $117.31/day as of February 2026): average monthly income equivalent to ~400 UMA days (~MXN $46,924/month) for 6 months; OR average monthly bank balance of ~20,000 UMA days (~MXN $2,346,200) for 12 months; OR real property in Mexico exceeding ~40,000 UMA days (~MXN $4,692,400) in assessed value. Grants up to 4 years temporary residency, renewable. After 4 years can apply for Permanent Residency.

visa_types.name: Temporary Resident Visa for Investors (Residente Temporal - Inversión)
visa_types.purpose: Allows foreign nationals who have made qualifying investments in Mexico to reside there on a temporary basis for up to 4 years.
visa_types.notes: Investment threshold: equity stake, assets, or business activity exceeding approximately MXN $5,378,663 (45,850 UMA days at $117.31/day as of February 2026; approximately EUR 256,127 per Belgium embassy page). Can also qualify by employing at least 3 Mexican workers. Visa must be used within 180 days of issuance. Does not authorize paid employment in Mexico. Must apply for Temporary Resident Card at INM within 30 days of arrival. After 4 years of temporary residency can apply for Permanent Residency.

visa_types.name: Temporary Resident Visa - Family Unity (Residente Temporal - Unidad Familiar / Vínculo Familiar)
visa_types.purpose: Allows immediate family members (spouse, children, dependent parents) of Mexican citizens, permanent residents, or temporary residents to live in Mexico under family reunification.
visa_types.notes: Issued to spouses, children, and dependent parents of Mexican nationals or of foreigners holding temporary or permanent resident status. Duration mirrors the principal holder's residency or up to 4 years. Holder must apply for Temporary Resident Card at INM within 30 days of arrival. Can lead to Permanent Residency after required period.

visa_types.name: Permanent Resident Visa (Visa de Residente Permanente)
visa_types.purpose: Grants indefinite authorization to reside in Mexico without the need for periodic renewal, available to those who have completed 4 years as a Temporary Resident, qualify through marriage to a Mexican national, or meet the economic solvency threshold for permanent residency.
visa_types.notes: Pathways to permanent residency include: (1) completing 4 consecutive years as a Temporary Resident; (2) being the spouse or dependent child of a Mexican citizen; (3) economic solvency - requires average monthly bank balance exceeding approximately $292,859 USD (12-month period). Grants indefinite right of residence. Work authorization included. After the required period of actual physical residence, permanent residents may apply for Mexican nationality by naturalization.

visa_types.name: Diplomatic and Official Visa (Visa Diplomática / Visa Oficial)
visa_types.purpose: Issued to holders of diplomatic, official, service, or consular passports traveling to Mexico on official missions or private visits, under bilateral agreements between Mexico and the issuing country.
visa_types.notes: No consular fee applies. Many countries' diplomatic/official/service passport holders are visa-exempt under bilateral agreements (see conditional_access entries). Where a visa is required, it is issued within 1 working day of submitting complete documentation. A verbal note from the applicant's diplomatic representation is required. US diplomatic/official passport holders receive 180 days (not 90). Pakistan diplomatic passport holders receive 3 months. Passport must remain valid from entry date onward.

visa_types.name: Visa Electrónica / SAE (Sistema de Autorización Electrónica)
visa_types.purpose: An electronic visa (officially called 'Visa Electrónica' by the SRE) required for certain nationalities traveling to Mexico by air. Applied for online before travel; classified as e_visa not ETA because the SRE itself calls it a visa.
visa_types.notes: Currently covers: Brazil (air travel only, effective February 5, 2026; 180 days max stay); Russia, Turkey, Ukraine (air travel only; stay duration determined by immigration officer at port of entry, not fixed by the document). Authorization valid 30 days from issuance. Single entry. Land and sea entry by these nationalities still requires a traditional consular visa. Apply online at visaelectronica.sre.gob.mx. The SRE program page at gob.mx/sre/acciones-y-programas/visa-electronica-sae confirms this is officially called 'Visa Electrónica'.

visa_types.name: Working Holiday Visa (Visa de Trabajo y Vacaciones) - Mexico-New Zealand
visa_types.purpose: Allows young New Zealand nationals (aged 18-30) to travel in Mexico for up to one year while undertaking incidental short-term work or study to help fund the holiday, under the reciprocal Mexico-New Zealand Working Holiday agreement.
visa_types.notes: Reciprocal bilateral scheme. New Zealand citizens aged 18-30 inclusive at time of application, no accompanying dependents. Holder must not work for the same employer for more than 3 months and may take one training/study course of up to 3 months. Apply at the Embassy of Mexico in Wellington. On arrival the holder must register with INM within 30 days to obtain a one-year Temporary Resident Card. New Zealand was Mexico's first working-holiday partner; Mexico also has an in-force Vacaciones y Trabajo (Working Holiday) agreement with France (see separate entry).

visa_types.name: Regional Visitor Card (Tarjeta de Visitante Regional, TVR)
visa_types.purpose: Allows nationals and permanent residents of Guatemala, Belize, El Salvador and Honduras to make short, repeated visa-free visits to Mexico's southern border states.
visa_types.notes: Free of charge; valid 5 years with multiple entries. Each entry permits transit/visit of up to 7 calendar days limited to five southern border states: Campeche, Chiapas, Tabasco, Quintana Roo and Yucatan. Does NOT authorize paid/remunerated activities. Issued on the spot at one of seven designated southern-border internation points after biometric capture; no online application. Eligible: nationals of Guatemala, Belize, El Salvador and Honduras (and permanent residents of those countries).

visa_types.name: Border Worker Visitor Card (Tarjeta de Visitante Trabajador Fronterizo, TVTF)
visa_types.purpose: Allows Guatemalan and Belizean nationals holding a job offer to work legally in Mexico's southern border states.
visa_types.notes: For nationals of Guatemala and Belize with a written job offer. Authorizes paid/remunerated work with multiple entries and exits, limited to four southern border states: Campeche, Chiapas, Tabasco and Quintana Roo. Valid 1 year, renewable. Fee approximately MXN $581 (2026 rate, ~31 USD); applicants earning the regional minimum wage are exempt from the fee. Issued at designated southern-border internation points; not available online.

visa_types.name: Humanitarian Visitor Visa (Visa / Condicion de Estancia de Visitante por Razones Humanitarias)
visa_types.purpose: Issued to foreign nationals who need to enter or remain in Mexico for humanitarian reasons - e.g. victims or witnesses of crime, unaccompanied minors, asylum seekers, persons whose life or integrity is at risk, or those providing disaster relief.
visa_types.notes: Statutory condicion de estancia under Article 52(V) of the Ley de Migracion. May be requested at a Mexican consulate (consular authorization valid 30 business days to enter) or applied for / regularized inside Mexico at INM. Grounds include family ties where a relative is a victim of disaster or violence or is in a serious state of health, and members of relief/rescue organizations on temporary non-remunerated missions; applicants are also advised of the right to request refugee status on entry. The resulting card is valid up to 1 year and is renewable while the humanitarian cause subsists; the humanitarian-visitor condition permits paid work in Mexico.

visa_types.name: Adoption Visitor Visa (Visa de Visitante para Realizar Trámites de Adopción / Visitante con Fines de Adopción)
visa_types.purpose: Issued to a foreign national carrying out the adoption of a Mexican minor, authorizing them to remain in Mexico until the adoption is finalized and the child can lawfully leave the country with the adoptive parent(s).
visa_types.notes: Statutory condicion de estancia 'Visitante con fines de adopción' under the Ley de Migración (Art. 52). Applicable to foreign nationals who are nationals or habitual residents of a country party to the Hague Convention on Protection of Children and Co-operation in Respect of Intercountry Adoption, or of a country with which Mexico has a bilateral adoption agreement. Requires the adoptability/pre-assignment report issued by the DIF (Sistema Nacional para el Desarrollo Integral de la Familia) and acceptance of the assignment by the receiving State's Central Authority. No fixed stay length: the holder may remain until the adoption resolution is executed, the child's birth certificate is registered, the Mexican passport is issued and documents guaranteeing the child's admission to the adoptive parent's country of residence are obtained. Apply by appointment via the MiConsulado portal at a Mexican embassy/consulate; within 30 calendar days of entry the holder must obtain the tarjeta de visitante con fines de adopción from INM.

visa_types.name: Working Holiday Visa (Visa de Vacaciones y Trabajo / Trabajo y Vacaciones) - Mexico-France
visa_types.purpose: Allows young French nationals (aged 18-30) to holiday in Mexico for up to one year while undertaking incidental paid work to help fund the stay, under the reciprocal Mexico-France Vacaciones y Trabajo agreement.
visa_types.notes: Reciprocal bilateral scheme, in force since 1 September 2016. Reserved for French citizens (not third-country nationals resident in France), aged 18-30 inclusive at time of application; may be obtained only once in a lifetime. Requires proof of funds of approximately EUR 2,500 and health/medical insurance covering the full stay. Apply at the Embassy/Consulate of Mexico in France by appointment via the MiConsulado portal. On arrival the holder registers with INM within 30 days to obtain a one-year Temporary Resident Card. Both states may set an annual cap on beneficiaries.
